title: Viettrans.info: funding machine translation for minority languages

lines.speaker: Lan
lines.text: Thanks for joining, everyone. Today we need to agree on how to fund the next phase of Viettrans.info: machine translation for the ethnic minority languages of Vietnam.

lines.speaker: Hoa
lines.text: Some context first. Vietnam officially recognizes fifty four ethnic groups, and many of their languages have almost no text online.

lines.speaker: Quang
lines.text: To be honest, minorities are only about two percent of the population, so funders may see this as a niche problem.

lines.speaker: Lan
lines.text: I don't think that number is right. Let's check it before it goes into any proposal.

lines.speaker: Minh
lines.text: On the technical side, these are low resource languages. For Tay and Hmong we have maybe twenty thousand sentence pairs of parallel corpus, mostly from bilingual textbooks.

lines.speaker: Minh
lines.text: My plan is to fine tune Meta's NLLB model, then use back translation to create more training data from text that only exists in the minority language.

lines.speaker: Lan
lines.text: How will we know if the translations are good enough for real users?

lines.speaker: Minh
lines.text: We will report BLEU and chrF scores, and native speakers will rate a sample of translations every month.

lines.speaker: Hoa
lines.text: Native speakers are key. Village teachers in Ha Giang and Cao Bang already offered to help, but we need consent forms and a fair way to pay them.

lines.speaker: Quang
lines.text: On funding, we have three options: an AI for good grant, cloud compute credits, and a crowdfunding campaign in the community.

lines.speaker: Quang
lines.text: The grant I have in mind gives fifty thousand US dollars. With the dollar at about twenty thousand dong, that is one billion dong.

lines.speaker: Lan
lines.text: Let's double check that rate. Either way, the grant should cover data collection and paying the speakers first.

lines.speaker: Minh
lines.text: And compute credits can cover training. Fine tuning a distilled model should only need a few hundred GPU hours.

lines.speaker: Hoa
lines.text: One more thing. The communities should own their data, so I suggest we release the corpus under an open license, with credit to every village that contributes.

lines.speaker: Lan
lines.text: Okay, decision. We apply for the grant first, ask for compute credits in parallel, and keep crowdfunding as a backup for next year.

lines.speaker: Quang
lines.text: I will draft the grant proposal and the budget by next Friday.

lines.speaker: Hoa
lines.text: I will prepare the consent form and call the teachers in Ha Giang this week.

lines.speaker: Minh
lines.text: And I will share a baseline chrF score for Tay by the end of the month.

lines.speaker: Lan
lines.text: Great work. Let's meet again next Monday. Thanks, everyone.

suggestions.title: Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups
suggestions.body: The Kinh majority is about 85% of the population. The other 53 groups total about 14 million people (2019 census); Tay, Thai, Muong, Hmong and Khmer each number over a million people.
suggestions.trigger_quote: Vietnam officially recognizes fifty four ethnic groups
suggestions.more: Vietnam's 2019 Population and Housing Census counted about 96.2 million people. The 53 ethnic minority groups made up roughly 14.1 million (about 14.7%). The largest were Tay (about 1.85 million), Thai (1.82 million), Muong (1.45 million), Hmong (1.39 million) and Khmer (1.32 million). Many smaller groups have only a few thousand members, and several languages have little or no written material online.

suggestions.title: Minorities are about 15%, not 2%
suggestions.body: Vietnam's 2019 census counted about 14.1 million people from the 53 ethnic minority groups, roughly 14.7% of the population. That is a strong number for a funding proposal, not a niche.
suggestions.trigger_quote: minorities are only about two percent of the population
suggestions.more: Source: Vietnam's 2019 Population and Housing Census (General Statistics Office and the Committee for Ethnic Minority Affairs). About 14.1 million of 96.2 million people belong to ethnic minorities. Framing the project around reaching more than 14 million people, many in remote northern and Central Highlands provinces, makes the impact case far stronger.

suggestions.title: Low-resource languages
suggestions.body: Languages without enough digital text, especially parallel (translated) sentence pairs, to train translation models the usual way. Major language pairs have millions of pairs; 20,000 is very small.
suggestions.more: A parallel corpus is a set of sentences paired with their translations. Strong systems for major languages train on tens of millions of pairs. With around 20,000, the usual approach is to start from a multilingual pretrained model, add synthetic data (back-translation), and collect more high-quality pairs from native speakers in the domains users care about.

suggestions.title: NLLB and back-translation
suggestions.body: NLLB (No Language Left Behind) is Meta's open translation model family covering 200 languages. Back-translation turns monolingual text into synthetic training pairs by translating it with the current model.
suggestions.trigger_quote: fine tune Meta's NLLB model, then use back translation
suggestions.more: NLLB-200 was released by Meta AI in 2022, with distilled versions small enough to fine-tune on a single GPU. Back-translation works like this: translate text written in Tay or Hmong into Vietnamese with your current model, then train on those synthetic pairs in the Vietnamese-to-minority direction. Because the target side is real human text, output fluency improves even though the source side is machine-made.

suggestions.title: Does NLLB's licence fit our plans?
suggestions.body: The NLLB-200 weights are released under CC BY-NC 4.0, which forbids commercial use. That fits a community project, but ask whether any paid service or partner deal is planned.
suggestions.more: A fine-tuned model is generally treated as a derivative of the original weights, so the non-commercial terms carry over. If Viettrans.info later wants paid API access or a commercial partner, it would need a model with a more permissive licence or separate permission. Settling this before the grant application avoids surprises.

suggestions.title: BLEU vs chrF
suggestions.body: BLEU counts matching word sequences against a reference translation. chrF compares character sequences, so it gives partial credit for close word forms and spelling variants, which suits low-resource languages better.
suggestions.trigger_quote: We will report BLEU and chrF scores
suggestions.more: Both metrics compare model output with human reference translations, from 0 to 100. Minority languages often have spelling variation and several writing conventions, which BLEU punishes heavily. Meta's NLLB evaluation reports chrF++ for this reason. Automatic scores still need human rating by native speakers, as Minh proposed.

suggestions.title: Free, prior and informed consent
suggestions.body: Language data projects with ethnic minority communities often follow FPIC: explain the purpose in the local language, get consent before collecting, let people withdraw, and agree on pay and credit up front.
suggestions.trigger_quote: we need consent forms and a fair way to pay them
suggestions.more: Free, prior and informed consent is a principle from the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, widely used by NGOs and research projects working with minority communities. In practice: consent forms read aloud in the local language, a clear statement of how recordings and text will be used and published, a simple way to withdraw, and a payment rate agreed with the community rather than set by the project alone.

suggestions.title: $50,000 is about 1.3 billion dong
suggestions.body: On 4 Nov 2026, Vietcombank sold US dollars at about 25,900 dong (State Bank central rate 25,267), so $50,000 is roughly 1.3 billion dong, not 1 billion. Budget with the current rate.
suggestions.trigger_quote: With the dollar at about twenty thousand dong
suggestions.more: At about 25,900 VND per USD (Vietcombank selling rate, 4 November 2026), $50,000 is roughly 1.29 billion VND; at the State Bank central rate of 25,267 it is about 1.26 billion. The rate of 20,000 dong per dollar is more than a decade old. Grant budgets in dollars should state the exchange rate used and leave a margin for movement during the grant period.

suggestions.title: Is an open licence enough?
suggestions.body: Ask how communities keep a say after release. A licence like CC BY guarantees credit but allows any use; some projects add a community data agreement on how the corpus may be used.
suggestions.trigger_quote: release the corpus under an open license
suggestions.more: Open licences such as CC BY 4.0 let anyone reuse the data, including commercially, as long as they give credit. That maximizes impact but removes control. Community-centred data projects sometimes pair an open release with a governance agreement, or keep sensitive material (such as sacred or personal stories) out of the public corpus.

suggestions.title: Grant first, compute credits in parallel
suggestions.body: The team will apply for the AI for good grant first, request cloud compute credits in parallel, and keep crowdfunding as a backup for next year.
suggestions.trigger_quote: We apply for the grant first
suggestions.more: Rationale: the grant covers data collection and paying native speakers, the most important costs; compute credits cover model training. Crowdfunding is deferred to next year as a backup.

suggestions.title: Quang: grant proposal and budget
suggestions.body: Quang will draft the grant proposal and budget by next Friday.
suggestions.trigger_quote: I will draft the grant proposal and the budget by next Friday
suggestions.more: Owner: Quang. Due: next Friday. Use the 2019 census figure (about 14 million people) for the impact case and today's exchange rate for the budget.

suggestions.title: Hoa: consent form and teachers
suggestions.body: Hoa will prepare the consent form and call the village teachers in Ha Giang this week.
suggestions.trigger_quote: I will prepare the consent form and call the teachers in Ha Giang this week
suggestions.more: Owner: Hoa. Due: this week. Deliverables: a consent form (ideally available in the local languages) and confirmed volunteers among the Ha Giang teachers.

suggestions.title: Minh: baseline chrF for Tay
suggestions.body: Minh will share a baseline chrF score for Tay translation by the end of the month.
suggestions.trigger_quote: I will share a baseline chrF score for Tay by the end of the month
suggestions.more: Owner: Minh. Due: end of the month. Baseline before fine-tuning, so later improvements from NLLB fine-tuning and back-translation can be measured.

summary.summary: The team discussed how to fund the next phase of Viettrans.info: machine translation for Vietnam's ethnic minority languages. A claim that minorities are about 2% of the population was flagged; the 2019 census puts them at about 14.7% (14 million people). Minh plans to fine-tune Meta's NLLB on about 20,000 Tay and Hmong sentence pairs, add back-translation, and measure quality with BLEU, chrF and native-speaker ratings. Village teachers in Ha Giang and Cao Bang will help, with consent forms and fair pay. The $50,000 grant estimate used an outdated exchange rate (about 1.3 billion dong at today's rate). The team chose to apply for the grant first and request compute credits in parallel.
decisions: Apply for the AI for good grant first; request cloud compute credits in parallel; keep crowdfunding as a backup for next year.
Grant money goes to data collection and paying native speakers first.
Release the corpus under an open licence with credit to contributing villages.
